section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) as a 10-item measure rated on a 4-point scale, with an overall score computed as the mean of items after reverse-coding five items; higher scores indicate greater self-esteem. It reports internal consistency in the present study (Cronbach's alpha = .87 for women and .84 for men). The section does not mention study numbering, sample size, demographics, BMI, body appreciation measures, or survey method.
section_summary.evidence_source: "We included the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES; Rosenberg, 1965; Romanian translation: Schmitt & Allik, 2005), a 10-item measure of global self-evaluations of worth as a human being. All items were rated on a 4-point scale (1 = Definitely disagree, 4 = Definitely agree). An overall score was computed as the mean of all 10 items, following reverse-coding of 5 items. Higher scores on this scale reflect greater self-esteem." "In the present study, Cronbach ˛ for this scale was .87 for women and .84 for men."
